title: Patch: the AI expects the opponent to switch a unit from Defense back to Attack Position when its own evaluation prefers it
thread:
**Issue #4433 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4433: Patch: the AI expects the opponent to switch a unit from Defense back to Attack Position when its own evaluation prefers it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Before the AI picks its move, it imagines how you will answer on your next turn. In that imagined turn you can attack, use the abilities you have showing, and pull units back into Defense Position. But you never put a unit back into Attack Position, except with the three cards that have Deft. So a big unit you parked in Defense to protect it looks to the AI like a wall that stays a wall.

Example: the AI is at 8 life and you have a 9/9 in Defense. The AI may trade away its own Taunt blocker, or spend its removal somewhere else, as if the 9/9 will never swing. In fact you will flip it to Attack on your turn and threaten lethal.

Once this is built, the imagined you flips a unit back to Attack whenever that is the better move for you. The AI then weighs removing that unit, or keeping a blocker, the way a careful player would. Players notice it at the practice table, and against the ladder bots and the co-op AI team, which run the same AI.

## Why

- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:653-673` (`defense_switch`, #1696) tries switches only for units in Attack Position (the filter at 664-668).
- `deft_switch` (616-651) moves only a Deft unit out of Defense. Its doc says every other such unit stays in Defense.
- `lethal_wall` (681-713) only builds walls: `wall_switches` (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:1174`) skips units not in Attack.
- So an enemy unit that stands in Defense when the AI's line ends is still in Defense where the line is scored, at the AI's next turn start. There:
  - `face_threat_from` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:1455-1458`) counts no swing from it;
  - `unit_worth` (`evaluate.rs:676-683`) counts only `defense_attack_share` (0.5) of its attack.
  - No lethal-threat term ever reads such a unit, and killing it is priced at half its attack.
- §4.1 gives each unit one exertion a turn, an attack or a switch. A unit that switches to Attack cannot attack that turn, but it threatens the face from the next one. A real opponent switches back as soon as that is safe; the model never does.
- Scope: of the catalog's 369 non-token Units, all but the 32 printed with Can't Defend or Evasive can stand in Defense. Only 3 have Deft (core-045, meditative-031, stinkyscapeplus-029). Units reach Defense in three ways:
  - a player's own switch, every human's tool against a bigger board;
  - the AI's own stand-downs and walls (R1759000, R2976000);
  - cards that summon or transform a Unit into Defense Position.
- It mirrors two changes already kept:
  - #1696: the opponent switches to Defense when no attack is worth making. It was kept on its scene tests after a 199-199 screen.
  - #4210 / R4187000: the opponent walls up against lethal.

## Proposal

- In the reply's step 4, once no attack is worth making, `defense_switch` also tries switching the opponent's units in Defense Position to Attack:
  - units without Deft only (Deft stays with `deft_switch`, whose Defense already counts its whole attack);
  - only switches `legal_actions` lists;
  - in legal order, one node each, up to a new `AI_REPLY.attack_switches` (4; 0 turns it off);
  - weighed beside the Attack-to-Defense tries.
- `best_try` keeps a switch only when the opponent's own evaluation (`judged`, with the AI swinging next) beats standing still. So the opponent stays walled while the AI's board would punish it for giving up the Taunt and the Armor +1. A unit that switches has spent its exertion, so no reply flips one twice.
- A new ruling in this issue's block records the decision (Hearthstone has no positions). §9.9's reply paragraph and `crates/ai/README.md`'s description of the reply say it too.
- Screen it on improve-dev against `main`, and record the tally in the constant's comment, as #1696's is (R4319000). A screen whose edge interval lies wholly below 0 sets the constant to 0.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`: `defense_switch`, its doc, and the step-4 comment at 804-806.
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs`: `AiReply.attack_switches` in `AI_REPLY`.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`, plus any reply scene in `combat_mods.rs`, `pierce.rs` or `ranged_flying.rs` that stands an opponent's unit in Defense.
- `spec/09-architecture.md` §9.9 (The opponent's reply), `spec/rulings/R<issue>000.md`, `spec/pending/<issue>.md`; §4.1 for the exertion rule it relies on.
- `crates/ai/README.md`: the reply, under `decide` reads only `redact`.
- `crates/server/tests/fixtures/practice-claim.json`, recorded again if the AI's moves in it change, as #4173 did.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the AI's board empty and the opponent's 7/7 without Deft in Defense, `simulate_reply` ends with the 7/7 in Attack Position and the AI's hero untouched (the switch spent its exertion).
- [ ] With an AI unit on the board that would kill that 7/7 once its Taunt and Armor +1 are gone, the 7/7 stays in Defense.
- [ ] Deft units behave as before: `deft_switch`'s tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `leaves_a_unit_without_deft_in_defense_position_and_ends_its_turn` (`tests/ai/reply.rs:129`) pins today's behaviour. It is replaced by the new rule's test, named for the ruling, and every changed `counter.used()` assertion is explained in the pull request.
- [ ] A `decide` scene, failing on `main`, where the AI keeps its Taunt blocker (or removes the Defense unit) only because it now expects the switch back.
- [ ] A test shows that `AI_REPLY.attack_switches` at 0 restores today's replies.
- [ ] The improve-dev screen's tally is in the constant's comment.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo jackioh gate` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are green.

## Size and risks

- Small: one function in `reply.rs`, one constant, a ruling, the spec paragraph and a handful of scene tests. It is AI work, so `difficulty:hard` by CLAUDE.md rule 11.
- Node cost: a reply step whose opponent holds Defense units spends up to 4 more nodes once no attack is left, inside the reply's existing reserve. The perf gate covers it.
- Like #1696's, the screen will probably read inconclusive, since few of the dev set's deals turn on it, so the change rests on its scene tests.
- Every game against the AI plays slightly differently, so the practice-claim fixture may need recording again, as other AI changes have needed.
```
